text.p: Sequus Pharmaceuticals Inc said on Wednesday it had signed an agreement with Schering-Plough Corp under which Schering will exclusively market and distribute Sequus's drug Caelyx worldwide, except in the United States, Japan and certain small markets.
Caelyx is a long-circulating liposome formulation of doxorubicin, an anticancer drug.
In the United States Caelyx is sold under the tradename Doxil and is used to treat Kaposi's sarcoma in some AIDS patients.
Because Caelyx has received marketing clearance from the European Commission, Schering will begin selling the drug in certain European Union countries.
Under the Sequus-Schering deal, Sequus receives a $5.3 million up-front payment and could receive additional payments totaling $27 million based on targets and events.

As part of the deal, Sequus and Schering will jointly develop a worldwide clinical plan for investigating the use of Caelyx in the treatment of solid tumors. Each party will undertake clinical trials in specific indications, coordinated by a joint development team.
